TITLE: BenchPartner — Live Lab-Bench Copilot for the Data-Capture-to-Analysis Moment
CLAIM: A phone-first lab companion that rides along DURING the wet/physics lab — you photograph the apparatus and read measurements aloud, and it builds your data table, runs error propagation live, and flags anomalies ("your titration endpoint looks 0.4 mL off — re-check the buret") before you leave the bench, so your post-lab writeup starts from clean, defensible data.
RATIONALE: The lab-report grind has a structural failure: students discover bad/insufficient data hours later at writeup time, when the apparatus is gone. Existing tools sit on the wrong side of this gap — OpenEduCat/LabReportAI generate scaffolds/templates before/after; GradeWithAI/Frizzle/GradingPal are teacher-side graders. None is a contingent, live, at-the-bench organ responding to actual measurements as they happen. "Contingency beats content" applies directly.
STUDENT MOMENT: The 2pm lab-bench moment — recording messy measurements under time pressure, not knowing if your data is good enough until it's too late.
COMPETITORS: (a) Free ChatGPT/Gemini: can do error propagation if you stop, type numbers, and frame each question — but holds no live structured state of your experiment and can't flag a mid-titration anomaly. (b) AskSia does post-hoc lab math; OpenEduCat/LabReportAI/CoCalc are pre/post scaffolds — none live-at-bench. (c) Funded: AMBOSS ($298M) is med-clinical, not undergrad bench; no funded student-side live-lab product surfaced. (d) Research prototypes generate documents, not live anomaly detection. Open: the live, contingent, structured-state bench layer.
CHATGPT-PROOF: Persistent structured experimental state + live contingency + hands-busy capture. Chat is a blank box each turn; BenchPartner maintains your running data table, propagated uncertainties, expected-value priors, and interrupts YOU when a reading violates them. A stateful, sensor-fed loop, not a prompt.
CORE AI: Vision OCR for instrument readouts/handwritten notebook lines (robust-coarse: confirm-the-number, don't silently guess — flag low-confidence for a tap), STT for spoken measurements, a deterministic symbolic engine (CAS) for error propagation (no LLM hallucination on math), a small model maintaining expected-range priors per experiment type for anomaly flags. LLM only for the natural-language "why this might be off" hint.
INTEGRITY+TRUST: Does NOT write your discussion or fabricate data — captures YOUR real measurements and teaches error analysis (the high-order skill rubrics reward). A professor sees a tool that makes students collect better data and understand uncertainty.
